newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Sasol wary of Botswana oil-from-coal plan.
newsitem.headline: Sasol wary of Botswana oil-from-coal plan.

text.p: South Africa's giant oil-from-coal producer Sasol Ltd cast doubt on a planned $7 billion synthetic fuel plant in Botswana, saying the project was highly questionable.

Botswana media reports on Wednesday said a consortium of local companies led by Universal Investments (Pty) Ltd and Global Mining and Development Bank Botswana (Pty) Ltd were planning a multi-billion project to extract oil from coal.
Universal Investments president Jan Visser was quoted in Botswana media reports as saying the project would employ about 12,000 people and initially produce 2,000 barrels per day (bpd).
This would rise over the next three years to 75,000 bpd and then to 100,000 bpd -- which would rival the output from Sasol's Secunda plant in South Africa.
The Botswana project would be a joint venture with a large Romanian company and there would be close cooperation with synthetic fuel research organisations in the U.S., Germany and Japan.
Visser said the project would generate income of between $18 million to $20 million a month. He gave no further details.
But Sasol spokesman Alfonse Niemand said the project was questionable.
"The (Secunda) plant produces 100,000 barrels of crude oil equivalent per day. Its replacement value is around $10.5 billion.
"And at the prevailing price of crude, there is no way we would build another Sasol. The (Botswana) project...is highly questionable," Niemand said.
